newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo NBY plans no changes in money policy-c.banker.
newsitem.headline: Yugo NBY plans no changes in money policy-c.banker.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) plans no changes in its 1997 monetary policy with price and currency stability remaining its ultimate goal for the year, NBY first Vice-Governor Zarko Trbojevic said on Thursday.

"We shall keep the same profile of the monetary policy and the M1 money supply growth will only match the economy's growth, that is the planned 13 percent growth for the year," Trbojevic told a bankers meeting.
The M1 money supply rose to 5.8 billion dinars ($1.006 billion) in May from 5.495 billion dinars at the end of 1996.
"NBY shall stick to its basic principle to have stable prices and the stable currency and we plan to enter the next century with such policy," Trbojevic said.
Trbojevic insisted the central bank will do its best to keep the dinar exchange rate stable.
The dinar is officially fixed at 3.3 to the German mark.

"The dinar market rate has stabilised and ranges between 3.5 and 3.65...The stable exchange rate is our priority, it is not a coincidence but a result of a clear orientation of the NBY and federal and republican governments," he added.

Trbojevic said the central bank will continue to strengthen its forex reserves, but called on bankers to intensify activity to deblock substantial funds by Yugoslav banks and companies still remaining frozen abroad.
"Forex reserves can also strengthen with a more efficient collection of debt from our foreign partners," he said.

Trbojevic said it was high time for banks to restructure. "Our banks are sick and a radical action is needed to make them sound." He saw rehabilitation of the banking sector as a precondition for any economic reform. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4254
